entries.definition: Rank within the lane by CLR on the career workbook (by LPS on per-season sheets); Overview sheets rank across all lanes.

Career workbook: every team, league and lane a player logged, each shown with the CLR earned there and ordered high->low -- e.g. 'T1 (245.3), DAMWON Gaming (30.1)' (or shares like 'T1 (78%)' when built with --breakdown-pct). CLR is decomposed per year (its performance part in proportion to that year's LPS, plus the résumé bonus on the seasons that earned it) and re-summed per slice, so the parts add up to the player's CLR. Overview lists all lanes (so multi-role careers like Perkz/Xiaohu are visible); per-lane sheets list teams/leagues within that lane. NOTE: same-year team changes are booked to the season's primary team, so the per-team split isn't trade-accurate yet.

Career Legend Rating (career workbook only): the holistic, PPS/JAWS-inspired primary ranking = w_career*CareerVal + w_pace*PaceVal + w_peak*PeakVal + w_bonus*Resume. Blends career bulk, per-year pace, peak, and a titles/placements/awards resume onto one comparable scale so longevity, rate, dominance, and hardware all count. See the About sheet for the weights and divisor.

Resume bonus folded into CLR = w_bonus*(Intl + Titles + Awards), shown as its WEIGHTED contribution so CareerVal+PaceVal+PeakVal+Resume = CLR. Rewards big-stage results the box score can't see. Intl/Titles/Awards are shown post-w_bonus too.

International placement points from EVERY cross-region event LPS scores -- Worlds, MSI, EWC, First Stand, MSC, LTA, Rift Rivals, ASI, IWCI, IEM, IPL, MLG, DreamHack, OGN 2012 (champion / finalist / semifinalist / quarterfinalist / group), flat by event and round. Champion points are derived from the event's LPS weight (Worlds/MSI anchored), so a title's resume value tracks its on-rift importance. Credited to a player's team's finish that year.
Domestic split-playoff titles/finals (each scaled by that region's Elo strength that year -- an LCK/LPL title outweighs a weak-region one) PLUS domestic cups (KeSPA / Demacia).

Individual awards (regional/season MVP, All-Pro 1st/2nd/3rd, domestic Finals MVP, and at Worlds/MSI the Finals MVP + tournament MVP + All-Pro), a small tiebreaker, auto-pulled from Leaguepedia. Domestic awards are region-Elo scaled; the global Worlds/MSI honors are flat. Source: info/player_awards.csv.

Where the Resume score comes from, split into 14 categories -- each with a COUNT (#, how many the player earned across their career) and its WEIGHTED POINTS (Pt, already x w_bonus). The Pt columns sum exactly to Resume: Intl = WldsChmp+WldsFin+WldsSemi+MSIChmp+MSIFin+MSISemi+IntlChmp+IntlFin+IntlSemi, Titles = DomChmp+DomFin+DomCup, Awards = MVP+AllPro. Only SCORED achievements are counted (an unrated-region title scores 0, so it isn't counted). Points are region-Elo scaled where the parent bonus is, so two titles can carry different Pt.
Worlds championships won (count) and their points (flat, part of Intl).
Worlds finalist (runner-up) finishes (count) and points (flat, part of Intl).
Worlds semifinalist or quarterfinalist finishes (count) and points (flat, part of Intl).
MSI championships won (count) and their points (flat, part of Intl).
MSI finalist (runner-up) finishes (count) and points (flat, part of Intl).
MSI semifinalist finishes (count) and points (flat, part of Intl).

Other cross-region event titles (EWC, First Stand, Mid-Season Cup, LTA cross-conference, Rift Rivals, Asia Invitational, IWCI, IEM, IPL, MLG, DreamHack, OGN 2012) -- count and points. Champion points are derived from each event's LPS weight. Part of Intl.
Other cross-region event finalist finishes (count) and points (part of Intl).
Other cross-region event semifinalist or quarterfinalist finishes (count) and points (part of Intl).
Domestic split-playoff titles (count) and points (region-Elo scaled, part of Titles).
Domestic split-playoff runner-up finishes (count) and points (region-Elo scaled, part of Titles).
Domestic cup podiums -- KeSPA Cup (KR) + Demacia Cup (CN) (count) and points (weight-derived, part of Titles).
MVP-type awards -- regional/season MVP, Worlds/MSI tournament MVP, and any Finals MVP (count) and points (part of Awards).
All-Pro-team selections -- domestic 1st/2nd/3rd team and Worlds/MSI All-Pro (count) and points (part of Awards).

CLR bulk term = w_career * (CareerLPS / D), where D is a typical career length (yrs). Careers longer than D keep a proportional bulk edge; shorter ones scale down. Shown as the WEIGHTED contribution so the CLR component columns sum to CLR.

CLR rate term = w_pace * per-active-year LPS, empirical-Bayes shrunk toward the cohort mean by weighted games so brilliant short careers score well but tiny, noisy samples can't top the board. Length-neutral counterweight to CareerVal. Shown as the WEIGHTED contribution to CLR.

CLR peak term = w_peak * (mean of a player's PEAK YEARS + a length bonus). The peak years are the player's top k seasons, with k chosen to maximize mean(top k) + bonus*(k-th best season)*(k-1). A one-year peak scores its single best season exactly; a wide plateau scores its plateau average plus a reward for length, and a season only joins if it is close to the rest. A better season can never lower PeakVal. See the About sheet for the bonus value.
Number of PEAK YEARS: the top seasons that make up the player's peak plateau (always >= 1, since the best season counts). The width of the peak plateau.
Mean LPS across the player's peak years (the height of the peak plateau). PeakVal builds on this by adding a length bonus for extra peak years.

High Noon peer rank -- the player's BEST single-season standing, ranking rated players by that year's schedule-normalized LPS (1 = best that year). Lane = within their position; Glob = across all players/lanes. Companion metric, NOT part of CLR. Lower is better.

High Noon (3-year) -- the AVERAGE peer rank over the player's 3 best-ranked seasons (taken wherever they fall, not a consecutive window -- matching how PeakVal uses a player's best seasons), within lane / global. Captures dominance across a player's strongest seasons (e.g. ~1.0 = a clear #1 across three seasons). Lower is better; companion metric, not summed into CLR.
The seasons that make up HN3Lane / HN3Glob -- i.e. the player's 3 best-ranked years within lane / globally.

League Performance Score: total_score = Baseline + Contribution + WinBonus, accumulated across regular season, playoffs and tournaments (more games help). Schedule-length normalized (see About) so a full season is worth the same across years and these per-year totals sum to CareerLPS.

Pure mean per-game score (contribution + win-bonus + win-gated baseline), every game weighted equally, before the accumulation weighting -- schedule-length invariant and consistent with CareerLPS (baseline counts only on series wins).

WEIGHTED mean per-game score: total_score / total accumulation weight. Weights each game by its stakes (playoff/tournament games count more) but divides by the total weight, so it stays comparable across leagues. Above the pure mean => the player raised their game in higher-stakes matches.
Contribution component of LPS per game (pure mean, LPS scale) -- how much per-game value comes from win-prob contribution. Schedule-length invariant.
Weighted contribution per game = contribution points / total accumulation weight (same match scaling as LPS/Gm.wt). Above Con/Gm => the player's contribution was stronger in higher-stakes games.

INDIVIDUAL clutch = Bayesian-shrunk (high-stakes contribution/game) minus (regular-season contribution/game), using raw net_contribution. High-stakes = domestic playoffs + international tournaments; international games count 2× vs domestic playoffs (Worlds/MSI weigh more than LCK playoffs), and international games are further weighted by bracket stage (Finals=3×, SF=2×, QF=1.5×, group stage=1×). Bayesian shrinkage (k=20 games) pulls sparse samples toward the population median so noise cases don't pollute the ranking. Positive = raised their game in big moments; negative = faded. (Distinct from Intangibles, which is team-level and identical for all 5 teammates.)

LPS earned in each phase. Regular & playoffs are length-normalized per region (a full run ~ one unit); tournaments are weighted by viewership and normalized so a full winning run = the tournament's weight.
Points for the strength of the OPPONENT's league (cross-league parity term).

Win-probability the player added vs an expected player at their position (leave-one-out on Model 2), summed over games. Quantile-normalized PER LANE across ALL years (each lane's per-game distribution remapped onto a common reference), so the Nth-percentile game -- and the best-ever season -- is worth the same in every role. This removes the box-score bias that under-measures supports/junglers (making cross-lane and same-team comparisons fair) while preserving real within-year differences between lanes.
Credit for actually winning vs the model's expectation: beta*(result - p_model). Positive = won games the model rated as losses (clutch); negative = choked.
Contribution split by stat source -- these sum to Contribution. First blood is credited to the FB getter (+) / victim (-).
Mean per-game net win-probability contribution (after per-lane normalization; comparable across roles).

TEAM-level: mean per-game (result - p_model), i.e. how much the team wins ABOVE what its box score (KDA/damage/first blood) predicts -- macro, shotcalling, closing games, doing more with less. Identical for all 5 teammates (not individual).
Mean model win probability for the player's team-games (team strength).
Strength of schedule: mean opponent-league baseline faced (higher = tougher).
Share of games the player got first blood or was the first-blood victim.
Player's single-game best / worst net contribution (win-prob).
Distinct tournaments the player appeared in.
The player's home-region strength: that league's ending Elo for the year (see the Regions sheet). Higher = stronger region.
LPS earned at that specific tournament (WLDs=Worlds, MSI, EWC=Esports World Cup, KeSPA/DCup=domestic cups). These sum to Tourneys.
